summary: Review B (security) re-review of Phase S1 at ff361ff found no blocking defect. Step 9.4 now tells the author to check the Round 1 text for a secret value and to replace it before the report is written. This closes the open item from the c7d7e98 pass for Round 1. The new commit question fails closed: step 10 runs only after the user approves. run.sh and the tests are unchanged since 6e856e1, and both S1 suites pass. Three new nonblocking items and three carried test-harness items stay open.
security_applicability_reason: test-strategy.md section 5, Phase S1, says Review B is applicable with a short scope. The phase diff 65c7925..ff361ff adds agent prose that starts a subagent and commits its text (new-track.md step 9, spec-review.md) and an executable bash runner (tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh). The remediation diff c7d7e98..ff361ff changes the secret handling of the report and the commit approval.
nonblocking_findings: skills/measure/references/new-track.md:313 (same text in claude-skills/measure/references/new-track.md:313): the secret check of step 9.4 covers only the Round 1 text. Step 9.7 says 'Append the returned sections under that heading' with no secret check, and step 10 commits the Round 2 text too. The reviewer rule at spec-review.md:15 still reaches the Round 2 subagent, so this is defense in depth. Recommendation: add 'Check the returned text for a secret value as in step 4.' to step 9.7.

skills/measure/references/spec-review.md:86 (same text in claude-skills/measure/references/spec-review.md:86): the standard says the author 'writes the returned text without changes'. new-track.md:303 now tells the author to replace a secret value, and says 'without other changes'. The two files disagree. An author that reads only the standard can think that a replacement is not permitted. Recommendation: change spec-review.md:86 to 'without other changes, except a secret value that the author replaces with its file and line'.

skills/measure/references/new-track.md:303: the rule 'replace the value with its file and line' gives no form for a secret value without a known file and line, for example a value from the environment. Recommendation: add 'When the file and line are unknown, replace the value with [secret removed].'

skills/measure/references/new-track.md:318-322 (outside the security scope, for Review A): the option 'Approve the commit' says 'Continue to step 10'. The '## Accepted Risks' rule at line 322 and sub-step 9.9 at line 323 come after the option list. An agent that jumps to step 10 can commit without the Accepted Risks lines and without the estimated_tasks update. Recommendation: change the option text to 'Continue with the Accepted Risks lines and step 9.9, then step 10'.

tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh:29-35 (carried from the 6e856e1 pass, not routed): a pattern such as 'run.sh' or '*.sh' selects run.sh itself as a suite. The outer summary then counts the nested runner as one suite. This is an A3 count risk, not a security defect. Recommendation: skip run.sh in the match loop.

tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh:32 (carried from the 6e856e1 pass, not routed): '[ -f "$f" ]' follows symbolic links. A committed symbolic link below tests/spec_review_gate/ that points outside the folder will run. A pattern alone cannot cause this. Recommendation: add '[ -L "$f" ] && continue' or document the rule.

tests/spec_review_gate/test_s1_new_track.sh:22 and tests/spec_review_gate/test_s1_standard.sh:19 (carried from the 6e856e1 pass, not routed): 'TMP="$(mktemp -d)"' has no failure check. When mktemp fails, TMP is empty and the scripts write below the file system root. Recommendation: add '[ -n "$TMP" ] && [ -d "$TMP" ] || exit 2' after each mktemp call.
evidence: git rev-parse HEAD printed ff361ff9fcb0c93c6ab9998b4857f47df5885018, which equals audited_head_sha. git status --short printed only '?? extensions/' (out of scope).

The files are skills/measure/references/new-track.md, skills/measure/references/spec-review.md, their claude-skills copies, and measure/tracks/spec_review_gate_20261030/plan.md. The plan.md change is one line: '- Review remediation F1–F5: 54862aa'.
cmp of the two new-track.md copies and of the two spec-review.md copies printed no difference. The mirrors are identical. The suite check 'skills/measure equals claude-skills/measure' also passed.

Open item new-track.md:304 from the c7d7e98 pass is fixed for Round 1. new-track.md:303 now starts 'Check the returned text for a secret value (a key, a token, a password). When one occurs, replace the value with its file and line.' The check comes before the write, and the write comes before the step 10 commit. The replacement form matches the reviewer rule at spec-review.md:15.
The check is not complete for Round 2. new-track.md:313 appends the Round 2 text with no check (nonblocking finding 1). spec-review.md:86 still says 'without changes' (nonblocking finding 2).
The subagent handoff at new-track.md:302 is unchanged: absolute paths only, and 'Give it no secrets, credentials, tokens, or environment values.' spec-review.md:15 is unchanged.

New risk check, commit question (new-track.md:314-322): the question has two fixed options and free text. Line 321 says 'Step 10 runs only after the user approves the commit.' A free-text answer that is not an approval therefore gives no commit. The gate fails closed.

New risk check, findings question (new-track.md:304-311): the options are fixed text. The free-text answer goes only to the author agent, and it selects fixes in spec.md and plan.md. No text passes the answer to a subagent, a shell command, or a file outside the track.
New risk check, not-run form (spec-review.md:135-141): the remediation adds two blank lines only. The form holds no path, environment value, or user data.

New risk check, spec-review.md:69: the remediation removes the backticks around 'at most one re-review'. The meaning does not change, and the S1 suite check 'Re-Review Limit: one re-review and Accepted Risks' passed.

git diff --quiet 6e856e1 ff361ff -- tests/ exited 0 (TESTS-UNCHANGED). run.sh, test_s1_new_track.sh, and test_s1_standard.sh are byte-identical to the versions that the 6e856e1 pass probed. The earlier live probes of run.sh stay valid.
